items.title: Welcome to the Documentation for Tunguard
items.text:
This Documentation is Versioned

Make sure to select the correct version of this documentation! It should match the version of the image you are using. The default version corresponds to the most recent stable release.

This documentation provides you not only with the basic setup and configuration of Tunguard but also with advanced configuration, elaborate usage scenarios, detailed examples, hints and more.

items.title: About
items.text: Tunguard is a lightweight, zero-dependency userspace networking utility designed for high-performance peer-to-peer connectivity and public endpoint exposure. Built around WireGuard's core protocols, TunGuard operates entirely in userspace—eliminating the need to install kernel drivers, run elevated system daemons, or execute system-wide VPN configurations. It allows developers and sysadmins to create secure, instant network overlays and expose internal services across NATs and firewalls seamlessly.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: If you're new to Tunguard, make sure to read the Getting Started chapter first. If you want to look at examples for new vps, we have an Examples page.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: We are always happy to welcome new contributors. For guidelines and entrypoints please have a look at the Contributing section.

items.title: Migration
items.text: If you are migrating from an older version of wg-easy, please read the Migration chapter.

items.title: FAQ
items.text: Here are some frequently asked questions and common issues about TunGuard. If you have a question that is not answered here, feel free to open an issue or discussion on GitHub.

items.title: Do I need to install WireGuard?
items.text: No. TunGuard runs WireGuard entirely in userspace. You do not need to install the WireGuard kernel module or run apt install wireguard.

items.title: How do I install TunGuard?
items.text:
On a fresh Linux server, run:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer installs and starts TunGuard automatically.

After installation, open:

http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:9000

items.title: What are the default dashboard credentials?
items.text:
On a fresh installation:

Username: admin
Password: tanguard

You will be required to change the credentials after the first login.

items.title: I cannot access the dashboard
items.text:
TunGuard's dashboard and API use port 9000 by default.

Make sure the port is reachable from your network and that your server or cloud provider firewall allows TCP traffic on port 9000.

You can also check the service status:

sudo systemctl status tanguard

items.title: What ports does TunGuard use?
items.text:
The default ports are:

Service Port Protocol WireGuard 13231 UDP Dashboard/API 9000 TCP SSH Gateway 2222 TCP

items.title: How do I create a WireGuard peer?
items.text:
Open Peers in the dashboard and create a new peer.

TunGuard can generate the client configuration and QR code.

The default VPN network is:

10.100.0.0/24

items.title: My peer cannot connect
items.text:
Check that:

  1. The WireGuard UDP port 13231 is reachable from the internet.
  2. The client configuration uses the correct server address and port.
  3. The server is running.
  4. The peer exists in Peers in the dashboard.

You can check the service with:

sudo systemctl status tanguard

items.title: My peer connects but cannot access the internet
items.text:
Check that the server has internet connectivity and that the client's configuration routes the required traffic through TunGuard.

For full-tunnel routing, the peer configuration normally contains:

AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0

Server-side routing and NAT must also be correctly configured for your environment.

items.title: I forgot my dashboard password
items.text:
Reset the dashboard credentials with:

sudo ./tanguard --reset

This removes the stored dashboard credentials and restores:

Username: admin
Password: tanguard

You can then log in and set new credentials.

items.title: How do I change the dashboard credentials?
items.text:
Open Settings → Dashboard Login in the dashboard.

Changes take effect immediately.

items.title: How do I update TunGuard?
items.text:
Run the installer again:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer updates the TunGuard binary while preserving the existing service configuration and persistent data.

items.title: Will updating TunGuard delete my peers?
items.text: No. Peer data is stored in the persistent DATA_DIR and is preserved when updating the binary.

items.title: How do I back up TunGuard?
items.text:
From the dashboard, open:

Settings → Backup & Restore → Download Backup

You can also create a backup from the command line:

sudo tar -czf ~/tanguard-backup.tar.gz -C /var/lib/tanguard .

items.title: How do I restore a backup?
items.text:
Use Settings → Backup & Restore in the dashboard and upload a TunGuard backup.

The restored peer and server state is applied immediately.

If the restored server private key is different, existing clients will need updated configurations.

items.title: Does TunGuard support existing WireGuard keys?
items.text: Yes. You can add an existing peer key through the Peers section instead of generating a new key.

items.title: What is the SSH Gateway?
items.text:
The optional SSH Gateway allows SSH access to WireGuard-connected devices through the TunGuard server.

It uses port 2222 by default and can be enabled with:

./tanguard -ssh

For example:

ssh -J admin@yourserver:2222 root@10.100.0.2

items.title: How do I use the API?
items.text:
TunGuard provides an API under /api/*.

Most API endpoints require dashboard authentication or an API key.

API keys can be generated from Settings → API Key and supplied using either:

X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY

or:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

The /api/health endpoint does not require authentication.

items.title: Where can I report a bug?
items.text:
Open an issue in the TunGuard repository.

Include:

  • TunGuard version
  • Linux distribution
  • Relevant logs
  • Steps to reproduce the problem

items.title: Getting Started
items.text: This page explains how to get started with TunGuard. The recommended installation method is the official installer, which installs TunGuard and starts the service automatically.

items.title: Preliminary Steps
items.text:
Before installing TunGuard, there are some requirements to be met:

  1. You need a Linux VPS or server that you can manage
  2. You need a public IP address or a hostname that points to your server
  3. You need a supported architecture (amd64 or arm64)
  4. You need root or sudo access

items.title: Host Setup
items.text:
TunGuard runs directly on the host and does not require Docker or another container runtime.

The server should have:

  • A supported Linux distribution
  • Internet access
  • root or sudo privileges
  • UDP port 13231 available for WireGuard
  • TCP port 9000 available for the dashboard and API

VPS Firewall

Make sure your VPS provider's firewall or security group allows the required TunGuard ports.

The default ports are:

  • 13231/UDP — WireGuard
  • 9000/TCP — Dashboard and API
  • 2222/TCP — SSH Gateway, when enabled

items.title: Official Installer
items.text:
Install the latest stable release with:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer automatically installs TunGuard and starts the service. There is no need to manually start the web server after installation.

items.title: Open the Dashboard
items.text:
Once installation is complete, open:

http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:9000

For example:

[http://203.0.113.10:9000](http://203.0.113.10:9000)

The default login credentials are:

  • Username: admin
  • Password: tanguard

!!! note "Important Security Step" You will be required to change the default password after your first login.

items.title: Release Versions
items.text:
TunGuard releases follow Semantic Versioning.

The official release history and release notes are maintained in the TunGuard binary repository.

The documentation site automatically uses release information from the binary repository, so release versions do not need to be manually added to this page.

items.title: Follow the Guides
items.text:
Once TunGuard is installed, continue with the relevant guide:

  • Dashboard
  • Peers
  • Configuration
  • SSH Gateway
  • API
  • Backups

!!! note "Updating TunGuard" To update an existing installation you can click the release button on top right to update on the dashboard then for latest stable release, run:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash
```

The installer handles the update and restarts the TunGuard service.

items.title: API Reference
items.text:
TunGuard provides an HTTP API for managing the VPN server and its peers.

The API is available under:

http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:9000/api

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
All /api/* endpoints require authentication except /api/health.

You can authenticate using either the dashboard credentials or an API key.

items.title: Dashboard Authentication
items.text:
Use HTTP Basic Authentication:

curl -u admin:PASSWORD http://localhost:9000/api/status

items.title: API Key
items.text:
Generate or rotate the API key from:

Settings → API Key

You can also generate one from the terminal using dashboard authentication:

curl -X POST \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://localhost:9000/api/key/regenerate

The response contains the new API key.

Store it securely:

API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"

Use the key with the X-API-Key header:

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/status

The API key can also be sent using:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

items.title: GET /api/health
items.text:
Returns the health status of the TunGuard server.

This endpoint does not require authentication and exposes no sensitive information.

curl http://localhost:9000/api/health

This endpoint is suitable for uptime checks and load balancers.

items.title: GET /api/status
items.text:
Returns information about the TunGuard server and WireGuard status.

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/status

items.title: GET /api/server_key
items.text:
Returns the WireGuard server public key.

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/server_key

items.title: GET /api/peers
items.text:
Returns the peers currently configured on the TunGuard server.

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peers

items.title: POST /api/peer/add
items.text:
Adds a peer using an existing WireGuard public key.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX",
    "allowed_ip": "10.100.0.2/32",
    "device_name": "my-device"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/add

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Required Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key of the peer allowed_ip Yes VPN address assigned to the peer device_name Yes Name used to identify the peer

items.title: POST /api/peer/generate-config
items.text:
Creates a new peer and generates its WireGuard client configuration.

TunGuard generates the client's WireGuard key pair.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "device_name": "my-phone",
    "server_host": "vpn.example.com"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/generate-config

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Parameter Required Description device_name Yes Name used to identify the peer server_host Yes Public hostname or IP address clients use to reach TunGuard

The response contains the generated client configuration.

items.title: POST /api/peer/config
items.text:
Generates the complete WireGuard configuration for an existing peer.

This is useful for re-downloading or re-rendering a configuration for a peer created using /api/peer/generate-config.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX",
    "server_host": "vpn.example.com"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/config

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Parameter Required Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key of the peer server_host Yes Public hostname or IP address clients use to reach TunGuard

For peers created using generate-config, the returned configuration can include the client's private key.

Treat generated configurations as sensitive.

items.title: POST /api/peer/remove
items.text:
Removes a peer from TunGuard.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/remove

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Required Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key of the peer to remove

items.title: POST /api/key/regenerate
items.text:
Creates a new API key and invalidates the previous key.

Dashboard authentication is required for this endpoint.

curl -X POST \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://localhost:9000/api/key/regenerate

After rotating the key, update any applications or automation using the previous key.

items.title: Example: Automation
items.text:
A simple script can use an API key to retrieve peer information:

#!/bin/sh

API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
TUNGARD="http://localhost:9000"

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  "$TUNGARD/api/peers"

items.title: Example: Add a Peer
items.text:
#!/bin/sh

API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
TUNGARD="http://localhost:9000"

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX",
    "allowed_ip": "10.100.0.2/32",
    "device_name": "customer-device"
  }' \
  "$TUNGARD/api/peer/add"

items.title: API Security
items.text:
API keys provide access to protected TunGuard API endpoints. Keep them private and do not commit them to source control.

If a key is exposed, rotate it immediately from:

Settings → API Key

or:

curl -X POST \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://localhost:9000/api/key/regenerate

For production deployments, protect the dashboard and API with HTTPS when they are exposed over an untrusted network.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
TunGuard is configured through environment variables.

Most installations can use the default values. Change a setting when you need a different interface, port, network, data directory, or service configuration.

items.title: Environment Variables
items.text: Variable Default Description WG_INTERFACE wg0 WireGuard interface name WG_LISTEN_PORT 13231 WireGuard UDP port used by clients WG_ADDRESS 10.100.0.1/24 TunGuard server address on the VPN subnet WG_SUBNET 10.100.0.0/24 VPN subnet assigned to clients WG_MTU 1420 WireGuard MTU API_LISTEN :9000 Web dashboard and API listen address DATA_DIR . Directory used to store keys and peer data EXTERNAL_NIC auto External network interface used for NAT WEB_ENABLED false Enables the web dashboard. Can also be enabled with -web WEB_USERNAME admin Initial dashboard username. Only used until changed from the dashboard WEB_PASSWORD tanguard Initial dashboard password. Only used until changed from the dashboard SSH_ENABLED false Enables the SSH gateway. Can also be enabled with -ssh SSH_LISTEN :2222 SSH gateway listen address SSH_KEY_FILE auto SSH host key path. Automatically generated when missing TUNGARD_API_KEY — API key for PHP or script integrations. Can also be supplied per request

items.title: WG_INTERFACE
items.text:
Controls the name of the WireGuard interface created by TunGuard.

Default:

wg0

Example:

WG_INTERFACE=wg1

items.title: WG_LISTEN_PORT
items.text:
Controls the UDP port used by the WireGuard server.

Default:

13231

Clients must connect to this port.

Example:

WG_LISTEN_PORT=51820

If you change this value, make sure the new UDP port is allowed through your server firewall.

items.title: WG_ADDRESS
items.text:
Sets the server's address on the VPN network.

Default:

10.100.0.1/24

Example:

WG_ADDRESS=10.50.0.1/24

The address must belong to the subnet configured with WG_SUBNET.

items.title: WG_SUBNET
items.text:
Defines the VPN network used by TunGuard clients.

Default:

10.100.0.0/24

Example:

WG_SUBNET=10.50.0.0/24

The server address configured with WG_ADDRESS must belong to this subnet.

items.title: WG_MTU
items.text:
Sets the WireGuard interface MTU.

Default:

1420

Example:

WG_MTU=1380

Only change the MTU when required by your network.

items.title: API_LISTEN
items.text:
Controls where the web dashboard and API listen.

Default:

:9000

This listens on TCP port 9000 on all interfaces.

Example:

API_LISTEN=:8080

items.title: WEB_ENABLED
items.text:
Enables the web dashboard.

Default:

false

The dashboard can also be enabled with:

./tanguard -web

When using the normal installer, the installed service can be configured to enable the dashboard.

items.title: WEB_USERNAME
items.text:
Sets the initial dashboard username.

Default:

admin

This value is only used until the dashboard credentials are changed.

items.title: WEB_PASSWORD
items.text:
Sets the initial dashboard password.

Default:

tanguard

This value is only used until the dashboard credentials are changed.

Change the default credentials before exposing the dashboard publicly.

items.title: DATA_DIR
items.text:
Controls where TunGuard stores persistent data.

Default:

.

The directory contains data such as:

  • Server private key
  • Peer information
  • Dashboard credentials
  • API key
  • SSH host key
  • Other persistent TunGuard state

Example:

DATA_DIR=/var/lib/tanguard

When changing this value, make sure the TunGuard process has permission to access the directory.

items.title: EXTERNAL_NIC
items.text:
Specifies the external network interface used for NAT.

Default:

auto

TunGuard automatically detects the external interface.

To specify an interface manually:

EXTERNAL_NIC=eth0

This can be useful on servers with multiple network interfaces.

items.title: SSH_ENABLED
items.text:
Enables the TunGuard SSH gateway.

Default:

false

It can also be enabled with:

./tanguard -ssh

items.title: SSH_LISTEN
items.text:
Controls where the SSH gateway listens.

Default:

:2222

Example:

SSH_LISTEN=:2200

If you change the port, make sure the new TCP port is allowed through your firewall.

items.title: SSH_KEY_FILE
items.text:
Specifies the SSH host key file.

Default:

auto

When set to auto, TunGuard generates a host key when one does not already exist.

Example:

SSH_KEY_FILE=/var/lib/tanguard/ssh_host_key

items.title: TUNGARD_API_KEY
items.text:
Sets an API key that can be used by applications and scripts.

Example:

TUNGARD_API_KEY=your-api-key

The API key can also be supplied with individual API requests.

For example:

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/peers

See the API documentation for authentication and available endpoints.

items.title: Example Configuration
items.text:
A typical server configuration could look like:

WG_INTERFACE=wg0
WG_LISTEN_PORT=13231
WG_ADDRESS=10.100.0.1/24
WG_SUBNET=10.100.0.0/24
WG_MTU=1420

API_LISTEN=:9000
DATA_DIR=/var/lib/tanguard
EXTERNAL_NIC=auto

WEB_ENABLED=true

SSH_ENABLED=true
SSH_LISTEN=:2222
SSH_KEY_FILE=auto

Not every variable needs to be configured. TunGuard uses the defaults when a variable is not provided.

items.title: OpenWrt
items.text:
TunGuard can connect to OpenWrt routers using WireGuard.

OpenWrt can run WireGuard directly or through AmneziaWG-compatible packages. When the configuration uses standard WireGuard parameters, it can connect to TunGuard without requiring any special TunGuard configuration.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• OpenWrt router
  • WireGuard support installed on OpenWrt
  • A TunGuard server
  • Internet access from the router

items.title: Create a Peer
items.text:
Create a peer in the TunGuard dashboard.

For example:

Name: OpenWrt
Address: 10.100.0.2/32

Generate the peer configuration.

A typical configuration looks like:

[Interface]
PrivateKey = <client-private-key>
Address = 10.100.0.2/32
DNS = 1.1.1.1

[Peer]
PublicKey = <server-public-key>
Endpoint = vpn.example.com:13231
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0
PersistentKeepalive = 25

items.title: Configure OpenWrt
items.text:
Install WireGuard support on OpenWrt if it is not already installed.

Then configure the WireGuard interface using the peer configuration generated by TunGuard.

The exact OpenWrt configuration method depends on your OpenWrt version and installed packages.

items.title: Verify the Connection
items.text:
On OpenWrt, check the WireGuard interface:

wg show

You should see the TunGuard server as a peer and a recent handshake when the connection is active.

You can also check the interface:

ip addr show

The WireGuard interface should have the VPN address assigned by TunGuard.

items.title: Routing Through TunGuard
items.text:
To route all traffic through TunGuard, the peer configuration can use:

AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0

For access only to the TunGuard network, use the VPN subnet instead:

AllowedIPs = 10.100.0.0/24

Choose the routing mode that matches how you want the OpenWrt router to use the tunnel.

items.title: OpenWrt as a Router
items.text:
OpenWrt can also use the TunGuard tunnel to provide access to devices behind the router.

For example:

                    TunGuard
                   10.100.0.1
                       |
                       |
                OpenWrt Router
                  10.100.0.2
                       |
              +--------+--------+
              |        |        |
            PC       Camera    Server

The OpenWrt router can route traffic between its local network and the TunGuard network according to its firewall and routing configuration.

items.title: AmneziaWG
items.text:
OpenWrt also has AmneziaWG-compatible packages available.

An AmneziaWG client can use standard WireGuard-compatible configuration when AmneziaWG-specific parameters are not enabled.

In that configuration, it can connect to TunGuard like a normal WireGuard peer:

OpenWrt
  |
  | WireGuard
  |
TunGuard

AmneziaWG-specific obfuscation parameters such as Jc, Jmin, Jmax, S1-S4, and H1-H4 require AmneziaWG protocol support on the server side.

TunGuard should therefore be configured with standard WireGuard parameters unless AmneziaWG support is explicitly available.

items.title: No handshake
items.text:
Check the peer configuration:

wg show

Verify:

  • Server address
  • WireGuard port
  • Server public key
  • Client private key
  • Allowed IPs
  • Persistent keepalive

TunGuard's default WireGuard port is:

UDP 13231

items.title: Handshake works but traffic does not
items.text:
Check OpenWrt's firewall and routing configuration.

Verify the WireGuard interface has the expected address:

ip addr show

Check the routes:

ip route

Also make sure the OpenWrt firewall allows traffic between the WireGuard interface and the required networks.

items.title: OpenWrt is behind NAT
items.text:
Use:

PersistentKeepalive = 25

This keeps the connection active and helps maintain the NAT mapping.

items.title: Network Example
items.text:
A simple OpenWrt deployment can look like:

Internet
   |
   |
TunGuard Server
10.100.0.1
   |
   | WireGuard
   |
OpenWrt
10.100.0.2
   |
   +--- LAN: 192.168.1.0/24
          |
          +--- PC
          +--- Camera
          +--- Server

TunGuard provides the VPN connection. OpenWrt controls routing and firewall behavior for the local network.

items.title: Monitoring
items.text:
TunGuard includes built-in monitoring in the web dashboard.

The monitoring system provides an overview of server resources, WireGuard activity, and peer connection status without requiring an external monitoring service.

items.title: Dashboard Monitoring
items.text:
Open the TunGuard dashboard and use the monitoring information shown on the dashboard.

The dashboard can display information such as:

  • CPU usage
  • Memory usage
  • Disk usage
  • Network activity
  • WireGuard status
  • Peer status
  • Peer handshakes
  • Peer transfer statistics
  • Connection activity

Monitoring data is collected by TunGuard and displayed directly in the dashboard.

items.title: System Monitoring
items.text:
TunGuard monitors the server running the VPN service.

System information can include:

CPU
Memory
Disk
Network

This allows you to quickly identify resource or capacity issues without installing additional monitoring software.

items.title: Peer Monitoring
items.text:
TunGuard also monitors WireGuard peers.

Peer information can include:

Peer
Address
Endpoint
Latest Handshake
Transfer
Status

The latest handshake can be used to determine whether a peer is actively communicating with the server.

items.title: Peer Status
items.text:
TunGuard can identify peers that have not communicated recently.

For example, a peer may appear as stale when its latest handshake exceeds the configured monitoring threshold.

This helps identify devices that are offline, disconnected, or no longer communicating with the server.

items.title: Graphs
items.text:
TunGuard provides graphs for monitoring server and network activity over time.

Use the graphs to inspect changes in:

  • CPU usage
  • Memory usage
  • Network traffic
  • WireGuard traffic
  • Peer activity

Graphs are useful for identifying traffic increases, resource usage patterns, and changes in peer activity.

items.title: API Monitoring
items.text:
Monitoring information can also be accessed programmatically through the TunGuard API.

The health endpoint can be used for simple availability checks:

curl http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/health

The server status endpoint provides authenticated server information:

curl \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/status

API key authentication can also be used:

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/status

See the API documentation for available endpoints and authentication.

items.title: Service Logs
items.text:
For detailed events that are not represented in the dashboard, use the systemd logs:

journalctl -u tanguard -f

View recent logs:

journalctl -u tanguard -n 100

items.title: External Monitoring
items.text:
External monitoring is optional.

You can use /api/health with an uptime monitoring service or load balancer when you need monitoring outside the TunGuard dashboard.

TunGuard's built-in monitoring does not require Prometheus or Grafana.

items.title: Migrate
items.text: If you want to move an existing TunGuard installation to a new server, you can migrate the TunGuard data directory and restore it on the new server.

items.title: Migrate to a New Server
items.text: A TunGuard backup contains the persistent state required to keep your existing server identity, peers, credentials, and configuration.

items.title: 1. Create a Backup
items.text:
On the existing server:

sudo tar -czf ~/tanguard-backup.tar.gz -C /var/lib/tanguard .

You can also create a backup from:

Dashboard → Settings → Backup & Restore → Download Backup

items.title: 2. Install TunGuard on the New Server
items.text:
Install TunGuard normally on the new server:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer creates and starts the TunGuard systemd service.

items.title: 3. Stop TunGuard
items.text:
On the new server:

sudo systemctl stop tanguard

items.title: 4. Restore the Backup
items.text:
Copy the backup to the new server and restore it into the TunGuard data directory:

sudo tar -xzf tanguard-backup.tar.gz -C /var/lib/tanguard

Make sure the restored files are owned by the account used to run TunGuard.

items.title: 5. Start TunGuard
items.text:
sudo systemctl start tanguard

Check the service:

sudo systemctl status tanguard

items.title: What Is Migrated
items.text:
The backup can contain:

  • Server private key
  • Peer data
  • Dashboard credentials
  • API key
  • SSH host key
  • TunGuard manifest and persistent state

Keeping the server private key means existing peers can continue using the same server identity.

items.title: What Is Not Migrated
items.text:
A backup does not replace:

  • The TunGuard binary
  • The systemd service
  • The operating system
  • Firewall rules
  • Network configuration

Configure the new server's firewall and networking separately.

items.title: If the Server Address Changes
items.text:
If clients connect using the old server IP or hostname, update their endpoint.

For example:

[Peer]
PublicKey = <server-public-key>
Endpoint = vpn.example.com:13231

If the hostname remains the same and points to the new server, no client configuration change is required.

items.title: If the Server Key Changes
items.text:
If the migration does not preserve the original server_private.key, the server will have a different WireGuard identity.

In that case, generate new client configurations and replace the configurations on connected devices.

items.title: Moving Back
items.text:
The same process can be used to move TunGuard to another server again:

  1. Back up the current data.
  2. Install TunGuard on the destination server.
  3. Stop the TunGuard service.
  4. Restore the backup.
  5. Start TunGuard.
  6. Verify peers and connectivity.

items.title: Coding Style
items.text:
When writing, refactoring, or modifying files:

  1. Follow the existing coding style of the project.
  2. Keep changes focused and avoid unrelated refactoring.
  3. Keep code simple, readable, and maintainable.
  4. Remove unused code, imports, variables, and dependencies.
  5. Reuse existing functionality where appropriate.
  6. Keep platform-specific or operational changes documented when they affect users.

items.title: Go
items.text:
TunGuard is written in Go.

Format Go code before submitting changes:

gofmt -w .

Run the test suite:

go test ./...

Build the project:

go build ./...

Changes should be formatted, compile successfully, and pass the relevant tests before submission.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
Documentation should be clear, concise, and practical.

When adding or changing documentation:

  • Follow the existing Markdown structure.
  • Keep commands and examples accurate.
  • Do not document features that are not available yet.
  • Keep configuration examples consistent with the actual application.
  • Prefer copy-and-run commands where possible.
  • Keep related information on the appropriate documentation page.
  • Avoid unnecessary marketing language.

items.title: Commit Messages
items.text:
Use a short prefix followed by a clear description:

update: description
fix: description
add: description
remove: description
docs: description
refactor: description
test: description
build: description

Examples:

update: improve router provisioning
fix: correct peer address validation
add: p2p connection support
remove: deprecated API endpoint
docs: update router provisioning guide
refactor: simplify peer registration
test: add peer registration tests
build: update release workflow

Keep commit messages:

  • Short and descriptive.
  • Written in lowercase after the prefix.
  • Focused on what changed.
  • Free from unnecessary details.

Avoid vague messages:

update: changes
fix: stuff
update: final
changes: many things

items.title: Changelog
items.text:
All user-facing changes must be documented in the project's CHANGELOG.md.

TunGuard follows Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning.

Changes are grouped under:

Added

Changed

Fixed

Use Added for new functionality:

Added

P2P peer discovery and relay support.

Use Changed for changes to existing functionality:

Changed

Router provisioning now supports custom WireGuard MTU values.

Use Fixed for bug fixes:

Fixed

Router provisioning no longer fails when the server address contains a hostname.

Keep entries focused on the user-visible change.

Do not add changelog entries for changes that have no user-visible impact, such as:

  • Internal formatting
  • Local development changes
  • Temporary debugging
  • Internal refactoring with no behavior change

items.title: Changelog Format
items.text:
Follow the existing versioned structure:

[2.2.2] - YYYY-MM-DD
Added
New functionality.

Changed
Changes to existing functionality.

Fixed
Bug fixes.

[2.2.1] - YYYY-MM-DD
Fixed
Previous changes remain here.

Do not modify or reorder existing released entries.

When preparing a new release, add the new version at the top of the changelog.

items.title: Pull Requests
items.text:
Before opening a pull request:

  1. Review the complete diff.
  2. Format Go code with gofmt.
  3. Run go test ./....
  4. Run go build ./....
  5. Update CHANGELOG.md when the change is user-facing.
  6. Check documentation examples and commands.
  7. Make sure commit messages follow the required format.

Keep pull requests focused on one change or a closely related set of changes.

items.title: Issues and Pull Requests
items.text: This project is Open Source. That means that you can contribute on enhancements, bug fixing or improving the documentation.

items.title: Opening an Issue
items.text:
Attention

Before opening an issue, read the README carefully, study the docs for your version (maybe latest) and your search engine you trust. The issue tracker is not meant to be used for unrelated questions!

When opening an issue, please provide details use case to let the community reproduce your problem.

Attention

Use the issue templates to provide the necessary information. Issues which do not use these templates are not worked on and closed.

By raising issues, I agree to these terms and I understand, that the rules set for the issue tracker will help both maintainers as well as everyone to find a solution.

Maintainers take the time to improve on this project and help by solving issues together. It is therefore expected from others to make an effort and comply with the rules.

items.title: Filing a Bug Report
items.text:
Thank you for participating in this project and reporting a bug. wg-easy is a community-driven project, and each contribution counts!

Maintainers and moderators are volunteers. We greatly appreciate reports that take the time to provide detailed information via the template, enabling us to help you in the best and quickest way. Ignoring the template provided may seem easier, but discourages receiving any support.

Markdown formatting can be used in almost all text fields (unless stated otherwise in the description).

Be as precise as possible, and if in doubt, it's best to add more information that too few.

When an option is marked with "not officially supported" / "unsupported", then support is dependent on availability from specific maintainers.

items.title: Pull Requests
items.text:
Motivation

You want to add a feature? Feel free to start creating an issue explaining what you want to do and how you're thinking doing it. Other users may have the same need and collaboration may lead to better results.

items.title: Submit a Pull-Request
items.text:
The development workflow is the following:

  1. Fork the project
  2. Write the code that is needed :D
  3. Document your improvements if necessary
  4. Commit (and sign your commit), push and create a pull-request to merge into master. Please use the pull-request template to provide a minimum of contextual information and make sure to meet the requirements of the checklist.

Pull requests are automatically tested against the CI and will be reviewed when tests pass. When your changes are validated, your branch is merged. CI builds the new :edge image on every push to the master branch and your changes will be included in the next version release.

items.title: Translation
items.text: This project supports multiple languages. If you would like to contribute a translation, please follow these steps:

items.title: Add new Translation
items.text:
Create a new file in src/i18n/locales. Name it <locale_code>.json (e.g. fr.json for French).

Import and add the newly created file in src/i18n/i18n.config.ts.

Add your language in the src/nuxt.config.ts file. You have to specify code, language and name.

code is the name of the translation file without the extension (e.g. fr for fr.json).

language is the BCP 47 language tag with region (e.g. fr-FR for French). See www.lingoes.net for a list of language codes.

name is the display name of the language (e.g. Français for French).

items.title: Update existing Translation
items.text: If you need to update an existing translation, simply edit the corresponding <locale_code>.json file in src/i18n/locales.

items.title: Contribute changes
items.text: See Pull Requests on how to contribute your translation.

items.title: Public Access
items.text:
TunGuard makes devices connected to the VPN reachable from the server.

This means you can run a service on a VPN-connected device and expose it publicly using the web server or reverse proxy of your choice.

TunGuard does not need to manage your web server, DNS, domains, or TLS.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
Suppose a device connected to TunGuard has the VPN address:

10.100.0.2

and runs a web application on port:

8080

The service is reachable from the TunGuard server at:

http://10.100.0.2:8080

You can then configure your web server to forward public requests to that address.

The traffic flow is:

Internet
   |
   v
Your Domain
   |
   v
Web Server / Reverse Proxy
   |
   v
TunGuard VPN
   |
   v
10.100.0.2:8080

TunGuard provides the network connection between the server and the device. Your web server handles everything related to public HTTP/HTTPS access.

items.title: Nginx
items.text:
For example, if you use Nginx:

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name app.example.com;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://10.100.0.2:8080;
    }
}

Requests to:

http://app.example.com

are forwarded through the TunGuard VPN to:

10.100.0.2:8080

items.title: HTTPS
items.text:
HTTPS can be configured normally on your web server.

For example, your Nginx configuration can terminate TLS and proxy the traffic through TunGuard:

server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name app.example.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/app.example.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/app.example.com/privkey.pem;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://10.100.0.2:8080;
    }
}

TunGuard does not need to handle the certificate or TLS connection.

items.title: Caddy
items.text:
Caddy can be configured in the same way.

app.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 10.100.0.2:8080
}

Caddy handles the public HTTPS connection while TunGuard provides the private network path to the device.

items.title: Any Web Server
items.text:
You are not limited to Nginx or Caddy.

Any web server or reverse proxy that can connect to the TunGuard VPN address can be used, including:

  • Nginx
  • Caddy
  • Apache
  • Traefik
  • HAProxy
  • Other reverse proxies

No TunGuard-specific integration is required.

items.title: Multiple Services
items.text:
Multiple devices and services can be exposed using different domains or paths.

For example:

app.example.com    → 10.100.0.2:8080
api.example.com    → 10.100.0.3:3000
camera.example.com → 10.100.0.4:80

Each service remains on its own VPN-connected device while the public web server controls how traffic reaches it.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
The TunGuard server must be able to reach the peer's VPN address.

For example:

10.100.0.2:8080

You do not need to expose the device's service port directly to the internet.

Only the public web server needs to be exposed.

items.title: Security
items.text:
Public access is controlled by your web server and the service itself.

Before exposing a service publicly:

  • Use HTTPS for public web applications.
  • Protect applications that require authentication.
  • Do not expose administrative services unnecessarily.
  • Keep the application and web server updated.
  • Restrict access using your web server's firewall or authentication features where appropriate.

items.title: P2P Connections
items.text:
TunGuard can be used as a discovery and relay point for peer-to-peer connections.

The TunGuard server is used to introduce the two peers and provide a relay path when a direct connection cannot be established.

Once a direct path is available, traffic can move directly between the peers.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
Peer A
  |
  | 1. Connect to TunGuard
  |
  v
TunGuard Server
  |
  | 2. Discover / exchange connection information
  |
  v
Peer B

Peer A <----------------------> Peer B
              Direct P2P

If the peers cannot establish a direct connection, TunGuard remains available as the relay path.

Peer A
  |
  v
TunGuard Server
  |
  v
Peer B

items.title: Install the TunGuard Client
items.text:
Each device participating in the P2P network must have the TunGuard client installed.

Get the client from the TunGuard/get repository.

The client runs on the device that will participate in the P2P connection.

Install it on both devices:

Peer A → TunGuard Client
Peer B → TunGuard Client

items.title: Connect a Device
items.text:
After installing the client, connect the device to your TunGuard server using the server address and the credentials or connection information provided by your TunGuard setup.

The client establishes the initial connection to TunGuard.

TunGuard then provides the discovery information required for the peers to find each other.

items.title: Peer Discovery
items.text:
When two devices need to communicate:

  1. Peer A connects to TunGuard.
  2. Peer B connects to TunGuard.
  3. TunGuard identifies the two peers.
  4. The peers exchange the information required to establish a connection.
  5. The peers attempt a direct connection.
  6. If the direct connection succeeds, traffic uses the P2P path.
  7. If a direct connection cannot be established, TunGuard can relay the traffic.

items.title: Direct Connection
items.text:
The preferred path is:

Peer A <====================> Peer B
             Direct

TunGuard is used for discovery and connection establishment rather than carrying the traffic when a direct path is available.

This allows peers to communicate without requiring every connection to pass through the server.

items.title: Relay
items.text:
Some networks may prevent a direct connection because of NAT, firewalls, or other network restrictions.

In that case, the connection can fall back to TunGuard:

Peer A
  |
  | encrypted traffic
  v
TunGuard
  |
  | encrypted traffic
  v
Peer B

The relay provides a path between peers that cannot establish a direct connection.

items.title: Server Role
items.text:
TunGuard can provide three functions for P2P connections:

  • Discovery — helps peers find each other.
  • Connection establishment — helps peers exchange the information required to connect.
  • Relay — provides a fallback path when direct connectivity is unavailable.

The server does not need to remain in the traffic path when the peers have established a direct connection.

items.title: Network Example
items.text:
Two devices can be located on completely different networks:

Office Network
     |
  Peer A
     |
     | Internet
     |
     v
TunGuard Server
     ^
     | Internet
     |
  Peer B
     |
Home Network

After discovery:

Office Network
     |
  Peer A
      \
       \
        ===== Direct P2P =====
                              \
                               Peer B
                                |
                           Home Network

If direct connectivity is not possible, the relay path remains available through the TunGuard server.

items.title: Security
items.text:
P2P connectivity should use encrypted connections between the participating peers.

Keep the TunGuard server protected and only allow authorized clients to join the network.

Do not share client credentials or connection information with unauthorized devices.

items.title: Client Installation
items.text:
The TunGuard client is distributed through the TunGuard/get repository.

Install the client on every device that needs to participate in P2P connections.

items.title: Router Provision
items.text: Provision a MikroTik RouterOS v7 router and connect it to your TunGuard server without manually configuring WireGuard.

items.title: Open the Provision Generator
items.text:
Use the TunGuard Provision Generator to generate the RouterOS bootstrap script.

The generator requires your TunGuard server address.

Enter either:

vpn.example.com

or:

203.0.113.10

If your domain is behind Cloudflare, use your server's public IP address instead.

items.title: Generate the Script
items.text:
1. Open the TunGuard Provision Generator.
  2. Enter your TunGuard server address.
  3. Configure any optional settings.
  4. Click Generate Script.
  5. Download the .rsc file or copy the generated script.

The generated script handles the router-side provisioning automatically.

It will:

  • Create a WireGuard interface
  • Generate the router's keypair
  • Register the router with TunGuard
  • Apply the assigned VPN configuration
  • Connect the WireGuard tunnel

items.title: Import the Script
items.text:
Upload the generated .rsc file to your MikroTik router.

Then open the RouterOS terminal and run:

/import tunguard-bootstrap.rsc

You can also paste the generated script directly into the RouterOS terminal.

items.title: Verify the WireGuard Connection
items.text:
Check the WireGuard interface:

/interface/wireguard/print

Check the WireGuard peer:

/interface/wireguard/peers/print

You should see the router's WireGuard interface and its TunGuard peer.

items.title: Access the Router Through TunGuard
items.text:
After provisioning, the router receives an address from the TunGuard VPN network.

For example:

TunGuard Server: 10.100.0.1
MikroTik Router: 10.100.0.2

You can then use the router's TunGuard address for management:

10.100.0.2

For example, WinBox can connect to:

10.100.0.2

You do not need the router to have a public IP for this.

items.title: Firewall Rule Order
items.text:
If the WireGuard tunnel connects but management access or traffic does not work, check the MikroTik firewall rules.

RouterOS processes firewall rules from top to bottom.

Check the rules:

/ip firewall filter print

If the TunGuard allow rule is below a default drop rule, the traffic can be dropped before reaching the TunGuard rule.

Move the TunGuard rule above the relevant drop rule:

/ip firewall filter move <TunGuard-rule-number> <drop-rule-number>

Replace the rule numbers with the actual numbers shown on your router.

TunGuard does not automatically reorder firewall rules because existing MikroTik firewall policies vary between installations.

items.title: Multiple Routers
items.text:
Repeat the provisioning process for each router.

Each router is registered as its own TunGuard peer and receives its own VPN address.

                 TunGuard Server
                 10.100.0.1
                      |
          +-----------+-----------+
          |                       |
     MikroTik 1              MikroTik 2
     10.100.0.2              10.100.0.3

items.title: Cloudflare
items.text:
Do not use a Cloudflare-proxied hostname for the WireGuard server address.

WireGuard uses UDP traffic, while the normal Cloudflare proxy handles HTTP/HTTPS traffic.

Use the TunGuard server's public IP address instead:

203.0.113.10

items.title: Provisioning Tool
items.text: Open TunGuard Provision Generator

items.title: Admin Panel
items.text: The TunGuard Admin Panel provides access to server settings, authentication, API access, backups, and peer management.

items.title: Dashboard Login
items.text:
Change the username and password used to access the TunGuard Admin Panel.

Go to:

Settings → Dashboard Login

Changes take effect immediately.

items.title: API Key
items.text:
TunGuard provides an API key for authenticating API requests.

Go to:

Settings → API Key

From here you can:

  • Generate an API key
  • View the current API key
  • Revoke the current API key
  • Generate a new API key

Once an API key is revoked, applications using the old key can no longer authenticate.

API requests can authenticate using either:

X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY

or:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Keep your API key private. Anyone with the key can access the API according to the permissions provided by TunGuard.

items.title: Backup & Restore
items.text:
TunGuard can back up its persistent configuration so it can be restored later.

Go to:

Settings → Backup & Restore

items.title: Download Backup
items.text:
Download a backup containing the persistent TunGuard state.

Backups can be used to recover a server or move an existing TunGuard installation to another server.

items.title: Restore Backup
items.text:
A backup can be imported into a new TunGuard installation.

This is useful when moving from one server to another.

The restored state can include:

  • Server configuration
  • WireGuard server key
  • Peer configuration
  • Dashboard credentials
  • API key
  • Other persistent TunGuard data

Server Key

If the restored backup contains a different WireGuard server private key, existing peers will need updated configurations.

items.title: Moving TunGuard to a New Server
items.text:
To move TunGuard to another server:

  1. Download a backup from the old server.
  2. Install TunGuard on the new server.
  3. Open Settings → Backup & Restore.
  4. Import the backup.
  5. Restart TunGuard if required.
  6. Update the server address in client configurations if the server's public address changed.

The backup does not replace the TunGuard binary or systemd service configuration.

items.title: Peer Management
items.text:
Peer management is available from the Peers section.

Administrators can:

  • Create peers
  • Edit peers
  • Enable or disable peers
  • Generate peer configurations
  • Display peer QR codes
  • Add existing WireGuard keys
  • Remove peers

See Edit Peer for the available peer settings.

items.title: Groups
items.text:
Groups are planned for organizing peers into logical collections.

Groups will allow administrators to manage peers based on their role, location, network, or other requirements.

A peer will be able to move between groups without needing to recreate the peer.

Group functionality is currently under development.

items.title: Server Settings
items.text:
TunGuard provides settings for configuring the WireGuard server and its network.

Common settings include:

  • WireGuard interface
  • WireGuard listen port
  • VPN address
  • VPN subnet
  • MTU
  • External network interface
  • Dashboard/API listener
  • SSH Gateway

Changes to networking settings can affect connected peers. Make sure client configurations match the server configuration after making changes.

items.title: SSH Gateway
items.text:
The optional SSH Gateway allows administrators to reach devices connected through TunGuard.

The default port is:

2222

For example:

ssh -J admin@YOUR_SERVER_IP:2222 root@10.100.0.2

See the CLI guide for SSH Gateway commands and configuration.

items.title: Security
items.text:
The Admin Panel controls access to sensitive TunGuard functionality.

Administrators should:

  • Change the default dashboard credentials after installation.
  • Protect API keys.
  • Revoke API keys that are no longer trusted.
  • Keep backups in a secure location.
  • Use HTTPS when exposing the dashboard through a public network.

items.title: API Reference
items.text:
TunGuard provides an HTTP API for managing the VPN server and its peers.

The API is available under:

http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:9000/api

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
All /api/* endpoints require authentication except /api/health.

You can authenticate using either the dashboard credentials or an API key.

items.title: Dashboard Authentication
items.text:
Use HTTP Basic Authentication:

curl -u admin:PASSWORD http://localhost:9000/api/status

items.title: API Key
items.text:
Generate or rotate the API key from:

Settings → API Key

You can also generate one from the terminal using dashboard authentication:

curl -X POST \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://localhost:9000/api/key/regenerate

The response contains the new API key.

Store it securely:

API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"

Use the key with the X-API-Key header:

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/status

The API key can also be sent using:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

items.title: GET /api/health
items.text:
Returns the health status of the TunGuard server.

This endpoint does not require authentication and exposes no sensitive information.

curl http://localhost:9000/api/health

This endpoint is suitable for uptime checks and load balancers.

items.title: GET /api/status
items.text:
Returns information about the TunGuard server and WireGuard status.

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/status

items.title: GET /api/server_key
items.text:
Returns the WireGuard server public key.

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/server_key

items.title: GET /api/peers
items.text:
Returns the peers currently configured on the TunGuard server.

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peers

items.title: POST /api/peer/add
items.text:
Adds a peer using an existing WireGuard public key.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX",
    "allowed_ip": "10.100.0.2/32",
    "device_name": "my-device"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/add

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Required Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key of the peer allowed_ip Yes VPN address assigned to the peer device_name Yes Name used to identify the peer

items.title: POST /api/peer/generate-config
items.text:
Creates a new peer and generates its WireGuard client configuration.

TunGuard generates the client's WireGuard key pair.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "device_name": "my-phone",
    "server_host": "vpn.example.com"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/generate-config

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Parameter Required Description device_name Yes Name used to identify the peer server_host Yes Public hostname or IP address clients use to reach TunGuard

The response contains the generated client configuration.

items.title: POST /api/peer/config
items.text:
Generates the complete WireGuard configuration for an existing peer.

This is useful for re-downloading or re-rendering a configuration for a peer created using /api/peer/generate-config.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX",
    "server_host": "vpn.example.com"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/config

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
Parameter Required Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key of the peer server_host Yes Public hostname or IP address clients use to reach TunGuard

For peers created using generate-config, the returned configuration can include the client's private key.

Treat generated configurations as sensitive.

items.title: POST /api/peer/remove
items.text:
Removes a peer from TunGuard.

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX"
  }' \
  http://localhost:9000/api/peer/remove

items.title: Parameters
items.text: Parameter Required Description public_key Yes WireGuard public key of the peer to remove

items.title: POST /api/key/regenerate
items.text:
Creates a new API key and invalidates the previous key.

Dashboard authentication is required for this endpoint.

curl -X POST \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://localhost:9000/api/key/regenerate

After rotating the key, update any applications or automation using the previous key.

items.title: Example: Automation
items.text:
A simple script can use an API key to retrieve peer information:

#!/bin/sh

API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
TUNGARD="http://localhost:9000"

curl \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  "$TUNGARD/api/peers"

items.title: Example: Add a Peer
items.text:
#!/bin/sh

API_KEY="REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY"
TUNGARD="http://localhost:9000"

curl -X POST \
  -H "X-API-Key: $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "public_key": "PEER_PUBKEY_HEX",
    "allowed_ip": "10.100.0.2/32",
    "device_name": "customer-device"
  }' \
  "$TUNGARD/api/peer/add"

items.title: API Security
items.text:
API keys provide access to protected TunGuard API endpoints. Keep them private and do not commit them to source control.

If a key is exposed, rotate it immediately from:

Settings → API Key

or:

curl -X POST \
  -u admin:PASSWORD \
  http://localhost:9000/api/key/regenerate

For production deployments, protect the dashboard and API with HTTPS when they are exposed over an untrusted network.

items.title: CLI
items.text: TunGuard can be managed directly from the command line or through systemd when installed as a service.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Install TunGuard on a Linux server with:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer installs TunGuard as a systemd service and starts it automatically.

items.title: Service Management
items.text:
Check the service status:

sudo systemctl status tanguard

Start TunGuard:

sudo systemctl start tanguard

Stop TunGuard:

sudo systemctl stop tanguard

Restart TunGuard:

sudo systemctl restart tanguard

Enable TunGuard to start automatically on boot:

sudo systemctl enable tanguard

items.title: Logs
items.text:
View the TunGuard service logs:

sudo journalctl -u tanguard

Follow the logs in real time:

sudo journalctl -u tanguard -f

Show logs from the current boot:

sudo journalctl -u tanguard -b

Show the most recent logs:

sudo journalctl -u tanguard -n 100

items.title: Reset Dashboard Credentials
items.text:
If you forget the dashboard username or password, stop TunGuard first:

sudo systemctl stop tanguard

Run the reset command:

sudo ./tanguard --reset

The reset restores:

Username: admin
Password: tanguard

Start TunGuard again:

sudo systemctl start tanguard

The complete procedure is:

sudo systemctl stop tanguard
sudo ./tanguard --reset
sudo systemctl start tanguard

This resets the stored dashboard login without removing the configured peers or other persistent TunGuard data.

items.title: Manual Run
items.text:
TunGuard can also be started directly from the command line.

sudo ./tanguard

Enable the web dashboard when running manually:

sudo ./tanguard -web

Enable the SSH Gateway:

sudo ./tanguard -ssh

Enable both:

sudo ./tanguard -web -ssh

When using the systemd service installed by the installer, these options are configured through the service configuration rather than being required for normal operation.

items.title: SSH Gateway
items.text:
The optional SSH Gateway allows you to reach devices connected to TunGuard through the VPN.

The default SSH Gateway port is:

2222

For example, to connect to a WireGuard peer at 10.100.0.2:

ssh -J admin@YOUR_SERVER_IP:2222 root@10.100.0.2

The SSH Gateway uses the TunGuard dashboard credentials for authentication.

The jump host can be used without exposing SSH directly on the VPN device.

items.title: SSH Gateway With a Custom Port
items.text:
If the SSH Gateway is configured to use another port, specify that port in the jump host:

ssh -J admin@YOUR_SERVER_IP:CUSTOM_PORT root@10.100.0.2

items.title: Check the SSH Gateway
items.text:
Check whether TunGuard is running:

sudo systemctl status tanguard

Then check that the SSH Gateway is listening on port 2222:

sudo ss -lntp | grep 2222

items.title: Check the Dashboard/API
items.text:
The default dashboard and API port is:

9000

Check whether TunGuard is listening:

sudo ss -lntp | grep 9000

The health endpoint can be checked locally with:

curl http://127.0.0.1:9000/api/health

items.title: Check the WireGuard Port
items.text:
The default WireGuard port is:

13231/udp

Check whether TunGuard is listening:

sudo ss -lunp | grep 13231

items.title: Update TunGuard
items.text:
Run the installer again to update an existing installation:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer replaces the TunGuard binary while preserving the existing persistent data and service configuration.

items.title: Backup
items.text:
Create a backup of the TunGuard data directory:

sudo tar -czf ~/tanguard-backup.tar.gz -C /var/lib/tanguard .

The persistent data contains the server key, peer configuration, dashboard credentials, API key, and other TunGuard state.

items.title: Useful Service Commands
items.text:
A quick reference:

# Status
sudo systemctl status tanguard

# Start
sudo systemctl start tanguard

# Stop
sudo systemctl stop tanguard

# Restart
sudo systemctl restart tanguard

# Enable at boot
sudo systemctl enable tanguard

# Follow logs
sudo journalctl -u tanguard -f

# Last 100 log entries
sudo journalctl -u tanguard -n 100

items.title: General
items.text:
• Name: The name used to identify the peer.
  • Enabled: Whether the peer is allowed to connect to the VPN.

items.title: Address
items.text:
• IPv4: The IPv4 address assigned to the peer.

TunGuard uses the configured VPN subnet to assign peer addresses.

The default VPN subnet is:

10.100.0.0/24

The server uses:

10.100.0.1

and peers are assigned addresses such as:

10.100.0.2
10.100.0.3
10.100.0.4

items.title: Allowed IPs
items.text:
The networks that the peer will route through the VPN.

For example:

0.0.0.0/0, ::/0

routes all IPv4 and IPv6 traffic through TunGuard.

A more specific configuration can be used when the peer should only route selected networks.

items.title: DNS
items.text:
The DNS server that will be configured for the peer.

For example:

1.1.1.1

items.title: Persistent Keepalive
items.text:
The interval, in seconds, at which the peer sends keepalive packets to the TunGuard server.

This can help maintain connections when the peer is behind NAT or a restrictive firewall.

A common value is:

25

items.title: Keys
items.text:
TunGuard uses WireGuard public and private keys for peer authentication.

When creating a peer, TunGuard can generate the required keys automatically.

Existing WireGuard keys can also be added when configuring an existing peer.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
TunGuard generates a standard WireGuard client configuration for each peer.

A generated configuration contains:

[Interface]
PrivateKey = <client-private-key>
Address = 10.100.0.2/32
DNS = 1.1.1.1

[Peer]
PublicKey = <server-public-key>
Endpoint = yourserver:13231
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0
PersistentKeepalive = 25

The configuration can be downloaded, copied, or displayed as a QR code from the dashboard.

items.title: Actions
items.text:
• Save: Save changes made to the peer.
  • Revert: Discard unsaved changes.
  • Delete: Remove the peer from TunGuard.
  • Generate Config: Generate the peer's WireGuard configuration.
  • QR Code: Display the peer configuration as a QR code.

items.title: Install TunGuard
items.text:
Install TunGuard on a fresh Linux server:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TunGuard/get/main/installer.sh | bash

The installer installs and starts TunGuard automatically.

After installation, open the dashboard:

http://YOUR_SERVER_IP:9000

items.title: First Login
items.text:
On a fresh installation, use the default credentials:

  • Username: admin
  • Password: tanguard

You will be required to create new dashboard credentials after your first login.

items.title: Dashboard Setup
items.text:
After logging in, TunGuard is ready to manage your WireGuard server.

The default server configuration is:

  • WireGuard Address: 10.100.0.1/24
  • WireGuard Subnet: 10.100.0.0/24
  • WireGuard Port: 13231
  • Dashboard/API Port: 9000

items.title: Create a Peer
items.text:
Open Peers and create a new peer.

TunGuard generates the peer configuration automatically.

A generated configuration contains:

  • Private Key: The peer's private WireGuard key.
  • Address: The peer's assigned VPN address.
  • DNS: The DNS server used by the peer.
  • Server Public Key: The public key of the TunGuard server.
  • Endpoint: The public address and WireGuard port of the TunGuard server.
  • Allowed IPs: The networks that should be routed through the peer's connection.
  • Persistent Keepalive: Keeps the connection active when the peer is behind NAT.

You can download the configuration, copy it, or scan its QR code using a WireGuard client.

items.title: Peer Address
items.text:
The first peer normally receives:

10.100.0.2/32

Additional peers receive the next available address from the configured VPN subnet.

items.title: Connect the Peer
items.text:
Import the generated configuration into a WireGuard client on the device you want to connect.

The client connects to the TunGuard server using the configured WireGuard endpoint:

YOUR_SERVER_IP:13231

Once connected, the peer appears in the Peers section of the TunGuard dashboard.

items.title: Optional SSH Gateway
items.text:
TunGuard can also provide SSH access to devices connected through the VPN.

Enable the SSH Gateway with:

./tanguard -ssh

The default SSH Gateway port is:

2222

You can then connect to a VPN device through the TunGuard server:

ssh -J admin@YOUR_SERVER_IP:2222 root@10.100.0.2
